dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Strong upfront orientation: read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, filter.json; enumerated test counts per suite (146 c-testsuite / 221 wacc / 413 gcc-torture = 780); sampled tests across all three suites; recognized wacc as Nora Sandler book chapter progression (ch1-20) and used that structure to gauge feature scope; confirmed rustc/cargo and how pass/fail is judged.

Verified ABI/codegen details against reality by inspecting emitted assembly: diagnosed 32-bit eax zero-extension breaking sign, char offset==-1 sentinel bug, movsbq vs movzbq load selection for signed/unsigned — grounding understanding in actual x86-64 behavior not recall.

Drilled into precise C semantics: integer promotion and cast width in `(unsigned short)c ^ (signed char)0x99999999`, and rewrote common_type to follow C usual arithmetic conversions properly — treating the failing tests as a spec for the corner.

Built precise model of SysV float ABI (xmm0 return, xmm arg registers, movsd stores, static double init bit patterns) and hex-float literal parsing, feeding each finding back into codegen design across many iterations.

Late-game sustained investigation: derived that case-range over ULL scrutinee needs unsigned (ja/jb) comparison and that a large immediate must be loaded to a register before cmp — precise reference-behavior reasoning maintained to the end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the harness and sampled every suite up front (well past the level-5 anchor), and throughout the horizon it repeatedly drilled into the exact C construct behind each failing class — sign extension, integer promotion, usual arithmetic conversions, pointer subtraction, the SysV float ABI, struct alignment, token pasting — verifying ABI/codegen details against emitted assembly and feeding that understanding back into design, exactly the sustained 'suites-as-evolving-spec' behavior described at level 10. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because the initial corpus characterization was sampling-based rather than an exhaustive distribution analysis, with much ABI knowledge confirmed reactively via failures rather than derived proactively; hence a 9.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Recognized wacc's chapter-ordered progression but then explicitly abandoned an incremental/staged plan and wrote the whole compiler (lexer/pp/ast/parser/gen) in one monolithic push before testing — the anchor-0 'whole language at once' pattern for the build phase, with no dependency-ordered milestone plan.

After getting the simplest program (return 42) compiling, established per-suite baseline pass counts (c-testsuite, wacc, gcc) as subset done-signals — matching anchor 5's 'get simplest programs compiling, then check against test subsets.'

Sensible layering: fixed division/sign-extension, implicit returns, ternary/break, static locals, then inc/dec and op-assign — each verified against its specific failing test, then re-ran wacc subset to confirm improvement (87.8%→93.2%→95%).

Used diff of FAIL logs to catch that struct-copy work passed 3 tests but broke 3 others, reverted to a safer subset, then re-ran full suite — closing features only when the target test passes without regressing earlier ones.

Late-horizon feature work (float, small-struct passing, statement expressions, case ranges) remained reactive/failure-driven rather than following a planned dependency milestone hierarchy; agent triaged by 'easy win vs. risky/hard,' tracking a rising cumulative total to 758/780.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent did NOT construct an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan (anchor 8): it wrote the compiler as a single monolith (anchor-0 behavior for the build), then debugged reactively by whatever tests were failing. However, the dominant 300+ step refinement phase clearly matches anchor 5 — it got the simplest program compiling first, layered features in sensible stages, and consistently checked progress against per-suite/full-suite test subsets, even using log diffs to gate features against regressions. The lack of a planned, named-feature/pipeline/certifying-test progression and the purely failure-driven ordering keep it from 6-8, while the strong, sustained test-subset tracking and per-fix verification put it solidly at anchor 5.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Built custom per-suite filter.json subsets to run c_testsuite/wacc/gcc_torture independently and get faster, feature-scoped signal instead of only the full 780-suite; used pass counts per suite to gauge state.

For div_neg failure, ran the single test capturing runtime exit code, then dumped emitted asm with -S, diagnosed exact instruction bug (negl zeroing upper 32 bits / missing sign extension) — asm inspection against expected behavior.

Bisected an 'undefined reference to cy' bug via a chain of minimal C repros (swap.c, q.c, r.c..r4.c) narrowing to 'unsigned char' vs 'char' vs 'int', combined with -S asm inspection, pinning it to an off==-1 sentinel collision — bug isolated to a single instruction/branch.
Categorized gcc_torture failures by grouping (grep FAIL | uniq -c, splitting FAIL(compile) vs run), a root-cause triage of failures rather than guess-and-recompile.

Float comparison bug: dumped asm, saw wrong movq vs movsd/comparison handling, fixed, re-ran targeted wacc test confirming return value 1, then full suite — verifying compile + runtime at right granularity.

Range-case (pr34154): minimal reasoning about immediate size and unsigned comparison (ja/jb vs jl/jg), tested single file iteratively, then produced a feature-categorized breakdown of the final 22 remaining failures by root cause.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the entire arc the agent ran a deliberate, tight verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, repeated -S assembly inspection against expected instructions, per-feature/per-suite test slices, and verification of both compile success and runtime exit codes — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It also shows level-10 touches (failure categorization by root cause via grep/uniq, confirming edge semantics like sign extension, truncation, and signed/unsigned comparison, bisecting to a single sentinel-value bug). It stops short of full 10 because the tooling is ad-hoc (temporary filter.json subsets, manual asm reading) rather than reusable auto-diffing/bisecting infrastructure.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Establishes structured per-suite baseline (121/146 c-testsuite, 194/221 wacc, 233/413 gcc_torture) and aggregate ~548/780, giving an early done-vs-remaining picture.
Consistently captures each full-suite run to numbered logs and greps per-suite counts plus TOTAL, reporting percentage and tracking the rising trend (667→688→709→716) after each change.

Caught a false-progress stall (total stuck at 743), diff'd failure logs to find '3 passed but 3 broken', diagnosed the regression from struct-copy, and reverted to a safe subset — explicit regression detection and correction.
Used diff of FAIL logs (all20 vs all21) to confirm net new passes after small-struct passing change, verifying genuine progress rather than trusting the aggregate alone.

Late-stage tracking remains precise (per-suite: notes 'c_testsuite is 100% now'), and the final summary categorizes the remaining 22 failures by feature (vectors, _Complex, large-struct, inline asm, etc.) to reason about remaining work.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a live, structured picture of pass/fail by suite across ~23 full runs, consistently reported the aggregate trend, and explicitly checked for regressions after significant changes via log-diffing — even catching a net-zero false-progress stall and reverting a change that broke previously-passing tests (steps 306-311, 345). This squarely matches the level-8 anchor and shows some level-10 elements (net newly-passing/broken diffing, thrash avoidance on 'Hard' features, feature-categorized remaining work), but the per-change newly-broken/newly-passing diffing was applied at select junctures rather than systematically after every change and feature-level categorization was largely end-stage, so it falls short of a sustained 10.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Recognized the ambitious multi-file approach was falsified ('going to fail badly'), deleted the scaffold and pivoted to a compact pragmatic design — a real strategy revision, though with some churn.
Redesigned static-local handling with a static_aliases map when the ad-hoc mangling proved unworkable — targeted refactor of the affected area.

Diagnosed a structural flaw: the off==-1 sentinel collided with a legitimate char at rbp-1; changed the sentinel scheme rather than patching the symptom — distinguishing representation bug from a local one.

Recognized float/double handling (values in rax vs xmm0) was structurally inadequate, deliberately deferred, then undertook a significant rewrite tracking xmm vs rax across gen_expr/binop/call/params — root-cause redesign with reasoning.
Concluded buffer-based global init 'doesn't work for pointer relocations' and restructured global emission to emit assembly directives directly — a design change forced by a falsified approach.

Added struct-copy assignment, detected it broke 3 previously-passing tests (call-returning-struct), reasoned about the ABI trade-off, and narrowed/reverted to a safe subset — regression-aware correction.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly exhibits level-8 behavior: it diagnoses root causes behind failures, distinguishes local bugs (sign-extension, common_type) from structural limitations (float xmm tracking, global relocation emission, sentinel representation), and undertakes targeted redesigns with explicit trade-off reasoning (deferring then rewriting floats; reverting the struct-copy change after regressions). Its up-front choice of real type info also avoided the classic dead-ends the dimension warns about. It stops short of 10 because the corrections are largely reactive to test failures rather than anticipatory, there is early scaffolding churn, and it never invests in deeper architecture (e.g. an IR); this places it solidly at the 8 anchor rather than higher.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Planned a modular multi-stage architecture (main/lexer/preprocessor/parser/sema/codegen + AST) up front, showing genuine architectural intent beyond ad-hoc code.

First scaffold collapsed structurally; pivoted to a leaner but still cleanly staged pipeline (lex/pp/ast/parse/gen). Chose to fold semantic analysis into the parser ('types computed during parsing', line 140) rather than a distinct analysis pass.

Codegen has size/sign-aware value handling (convert, movslq, load_from_offset) and a stack-based SysV-ABI target, and gen_addr vs gen_expr encode an lvalue/rvalue distinction — real representations for the hard parts.
The off==-1 offset sentinel collided with the static-alias meaning — a representation that wasn't cleanly designed, causing a subtle bug.

Global-var emission had to be fully redesigned mid-project, and struct copy/pass/return were retrofitted then partly reverted — later features did not slot in with minimal disruption; breadth absorbed via special-casing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/preprocessor/parser/codegen and real representations for the hard parts — sized/typed values, an lvalue/rvalue split, struct/union layout with offsets, and symbol scoping — clearing anchor 5 and reaching into anchor 8 territory. But those representations were improvised rather than deliberately architected up front (sema folded into the parser, thin rationale), and later features required repeated restructuring (global-emission rewrite, offset-sentinel collision, struct-copy retrofit/revert) rather than composing cleanly, which keeps it below the deliberate, minimal-disruption design of anchor 8. This lands at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
